raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation The DeepSeek V4.1 Torch prefill indexer materializes full-size BF16 intermediates for ReLU and head-weight multiplication before reducing scores across heads. This introduces substantial memory traffic and kernel-launch overhead. This change fuses the score epilogue for the supported 32-head CUDA BF16 path while retaining the existing GEMM. ## Modifications - Add a Triton kernel that fuses ReLU, head-weight multiplication, head reduction, and FP32 output conversion. - Preserve BF16 rounding after multiplication and reduction, and follow the CUDA Torch 32-head accumulation order used in validation. - Pass context-dependent score-row and score-head strides as runtime parameters to avoid per-length specialization of these strides. - Retain the Torch fallback for unsupported devices/dtypes, non-32-head inputs, and widths of at most one. ## Accuracy Tests Local validation on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: - 20 CP request-row mapping cases passed. - 24 scoring and epilogue checks passed with exact agreement. - Epilogue stress tests covering 18 shapes and 100 seeds per shape passed with exact agreement, including BF16 rounding boundaries. - 8 Prefill integration cases passed with exact raw-index and KV-slot writeback agreement. - 8 synthetic arithmetic/retrieval probes at approximately 32K and 64K context lengths passed. GSM8K, 1,319 examples per run: | Configuration | Accuracy | Request error rate | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Baseline A/A, run 1 | 96.74% | 0% | | Baseline A/A, run 2 | 96.36% | 0% | | Optimized | 96.59% | 0% | The baseline A/A runs show run-to-run variation. These results do not establish bitwise equivalence of complete generated outputs or replace representative long-context quality evaluation. The validation scripts were run locally and are not yet included as CI-registered tests in this patch. ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Setup - Model: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. - Hardware: 8 × NVIDIA H200. - Prefill: TP4 / CP4 / EP4. - Decode: TP4 / DP4 / EP4. - Prefill BCG: disabled. - Decode and router processes held fixed across comparisons. - ### End-to-end benchmark Primary workload: all input 65,536, cache hit rate 50%,70%,90%, output 512 tokens. Results are means of three runs with 512 requests each and 10 warmup requests per run. ### Trace before-rank0: before-rank1: cur-rank0: cur-rank1: ## Checklist - [x] Format code with pre-commit. - [ ] Add CI-registered regression tests. - [ ] Update documentation, if required. - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results. - [ ] Repeat accuracy and performance validation after rebasing onto current main. - [x] Follow the existing code style. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #41789037868](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41789037868) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41789037933](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41789037933) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #41789037878](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41789037878) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. Our actual measurement has confirmed that under the current Torch/CUDA environment, when width=1, the head dimension becomes a continuous reduction dimension. Therefore, it is necessary to retain the Torch fallback.

+"""Fused BF16 score epilogue with the CUDA Torch 32-head accumulation order.

+Context-dependent strides stay runtime scalars to reuse kernels across lengths.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _head_product(
+    scores,
+    weights,
+    row,
+    columns,
+    head: tl.constexpr,
+    width,
+    score_row,
+    score_head,
+    score_col: tl.constexpr,
+    weight_row: tl.constexpr,
+    weight_head: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    value = tl.load(
+        scores + row * score_row + head * score_head + columns * score_col,
+        columns < width,
+        0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)
+    weight = tl.load(weights + row * weight_row + head * weight_head).to(tl.float32)
+    return (tl.maximum(value, 0.0) * weight).to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _reduce_32_heads(
+    scores,
+    weights,
+    output,
+    width,
+    score_row,
+    score_head,
+    score_col: tl.constexpr,
+    weight_row: tl.constexpr,
+    weight_head: tl.constexpr,
+    block: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    columns = tl.program_id(1) * block + tl.arange(0, block)
+    acc0 = tl.full((block,), 0.0, tl.float32)
+    acc1 = tl.full((block,), 0.0, tl.float32)
+    acc2 = tl.full((block,), 0.0, tl.float32)
+    acc3 = tl.full((block,), 0.0, tl.float32)
+    # Four interleaved accumulators match Torch Reduce.cuh (vt0=4) exactly.
+    for group in tl.static_range(8):
+        acc0 = acc0 + _head_product(
+            scores,
+            weights,
+            row,
+            columns,
+            group * 4,
+            width,
+            score_row,
+            score_head,
+            score_col,
+            weight_row,
+            weight_head,
+        )
+        acc1 = acc1 + _head_product(
+            scores,
+            weights,
+            row,
+            columns,
+            group * 4 + 1,
+            width,
+            score_row,
+            score_head,
+            score_col,
+            weight_row,
+            weight_head,
+        )
+        acc2 = acc2 + _head_product(
+            scores,
+            weights,
+            row,
+            columns,
+            group * 4 + 2,
+            width,
+            score_row,
+            score_head,
+            score_col,
+            weight_row,
+            weight_head,

+            weights,
+            row,
+            columns,
+            group * 4 + 3,
+            width,
+            score_row,
+            score_head,
+            score_col,
+            weight_row,
+            weight_head,
+        )
+    result = ((acc0 + acc1) + acc2) + acc3
+    result = result.to(tl.bfloat16).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(output + row * width + columns, result, columns < width)
+

+def reduce_head_scores(scores: torch.Tensor, weights: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:

+            enable_fp_fusion=False,
+        )
